note: An inventory of bounded claims and the CI jobs that back them. `gates` are jobs the single required check ci-required needs, so they run on every pull request; `scheduled_gates` run only on the schedule or manual dispatch. Evidence of record is a CI run of those jobs on the pinned toolchain (each uploads its logs as an artifact retained 90 days); local runs are informative only. `evidence_run` and `scheduled_evidence_run` name the latest green run of the gates when the entry was last updated: a push run on main, and for the scheduled gates a manual dispatch run that may be on a branch whose tree equals main's (formal/README.md names the commit). Reference validation is textual, not semantic proof.

claims.claim: The Lean model gives seal binding and closed DAG/checkpoint history under its honest-signer assumption; every hash-dependent conclusion is in explicit-witness form (equal bodies, or a SHA-256 collision on the two specific framed preimages), the standard reduction to SHA-256 collision resistance.
assumptions: SHA-256 collision resistance (never assumed as injectivity; explicit collision witnesses)
Ed25519 unforgeability, stated as a hypothesis about which messages were signed
honest signer
model inputs are post-NFC (Unicode NFC is trusted)
Lean 4.30.0 kernel

claims.claim: Rust matches the executable Lean preimage oracle on a fixed corpus and tag inventory; this is sampled conformance, not a mechanized refinement proof.
assumptions: corpus covers the relevant drift
Lean model expresses the intended format

claims.claim: The production seal core (canonical serializer, LP framing, sha256 digest string, record/checkpoint preimages and hashes, signature message) is extracted from core/src by Charon/Aeneas and proved to compute the Lean model's definitions; the model's explicit-witness seal theorems are applied to it (equal hashes give the same body or a SHA-256 collision on the two specific production preimages). Partial correctness only (results when the extracted function returns Ok; a panic or error yields no hash); arithmetic overflow panics in every shipped profile (overflow-checks in release and server, default in dev), matching the model's failure on overflow. serialize()'s final from_utf8 and the PreimageFault-to-RecordError mapping are unextracted glue pinned by call-path checks; base64 (core/src/b64.rs) is excluded as off the hashed/signed path and covered by plan 011's Kani proofs; the verifier's decision logic is refined only in its claim kernel (see verdict-kernel-refinement).
assumptions: Charon/Aeneas/Lean 4.31 toolchain, mathlib and the Aeneas std models (pinned in manifest.json)
rustc (exact pinned nightly for extraction; 1.92.0 for builds)
NFC and SHA-256 as arbitrary functions (unicode-normalization incl. its ASCII fast path; sha2)
String/str UTF-8 model
overflow-checks enabled in the shipped profiles
Ed25519 as the model's Signed hypothesis

claims.claim: The verifier's claim kernel verify::verdict::decide_claims (every function it calls, including the seal-key and anchor searches, the revocation-mode, capstone and plan 009 historical conditions) is extracted from core/src by Charon/Aeneas and proved to return, for every claim and the requested one, exactly the Lean verdict model's decideClaim on any evidence state its checked facts correspond to (Refinement.Corresponds). The model's support-erasure and claim-order theorems (deleting supporting attachments never adds a satisfied claim and never changes a refutation, with fixed signed records, pins, policy and authenticated adverse evidence), Supports inversion, capstone prerequisites, committed-contradiction refutation and the historical results hold for the production results. Total correctness, standard axioms only (enforced per declaration of the verdict modules and the extracted kernel by ProductionAudit.lean). Not proved: that verify.rs computes facts satisfying the correspondence (signature, pin, join, Merkle-path and snapshot passes, counter-to-fact joins); that boundary is pinned by call-path checks and tested by the verdict oracle differential and the adversarial suite.
assumptions: Charon/Aeneas/Lean toolchain and Aeneas std models
rustc
String::is_empty model
verify.rs computes facts satisfying Refinement.Corresponds

proofs.symbol: deletion strengthens a required trust claim

claims.claim: The production RCP parser (CanonValue::parse via parse_typed/parse_document and every function it calls) is extracted from core/src by Charon/Aeneas and proved to return for every byte string of any length (Refinement.Parse.parse_document_total): no panic, arithmetic overflow, out-of-bounds index or divergence. Hypothesis NfcFits (the trusted NFC primitive returns representable Rust strings), never an axiom. The theorem holds in Aeneas' std model: Rust Vec capacity overflow (a panic above isize::MAX bytes, reachable on wasm32 by one string of more than about 2^29 UTF-16 units), allocation failure and stack depth are not modelled; the verifier rejects bundles over MAX_BUNDLE_BYTES (256 MiB) before parsing, while the options JSON and the standalone canonicalize export are uncapped and rely on their callers. Not proved: which documents it accepts or what they parse to (tests, fuzzing, the parser differential and plan 011's Kani families cover that), the error rendering into_public, and NFC's own panic-freedom. Supersedes the unverified Kani harness parse_never_panics as panic-freedom evidence. The parser mutants m60-m64 are run against the regenerated proof (the CI job formal-production) on every pull request.
assumptions: Charon/Aeneas/Lean 4.31 toolchain and the Aeneas std models (unbounded Vec capacity, infallible allocation, unbounded stack)
input size bounded by the caller (MAX_BUNDLE_BYTES in the verify path)
NFC as an arbitrary function whose outputs fit in usize::MAX bytes (NfcFits hypothesis)
SHA-256 as an arbitrary function

claims.claim: Kani proves, only within each harness's stated bounds, properties of the real Rust: base64url alphabet bijection; base64url tail and 4-symbol chunk canonicality over the full per-chunk domains (whole-string uniqueness is argued in prose from the chunking, not proved); sha256:<hex> digest-string injectivity and canonicality per byte; exact LP framing; member-key order equal to UTF-16 code-unit order for keys of one or two scalars (5 of 5 harnesses) and transitive for single-scalar keys; the strict UTF-16 decoder equal to std's on every 1- and 2-unit sequence; the typed integer round trip for every n in [-99,999, 99,999]; canonical spelling of every accepted numeric literal of 1 to 4 bytes (61 of 61 shards); write_string then the real parser (real NFC) returns exactly Str(s) for every string of at most two scalars from ASCII, U+00E9 and U+1F600, exhaustively over the exact 17,031-case domain. CI runs every harness above on each pull request (formal-kani, formal-kani-extended) except the string family, of which pull requests run a 20-case smoke subset and the weekly schedule runs all 17,031 cases (formal-kani-strings-ascii, -mixed, -pure); the string claim rests on the latest green weekly run. Every Kani-detected mutant (m2-m4, m9-m13, m22-m25) must be refuted by its named harness on each pull request (formal-mutants-fast); all 48 mutants run nightly (formal-mutants-full). Not claimed: parse_never_panics (not verified; parser panic-freedom is the parser-totality claim).
assumptions: harness bounds and feature selections in run-kani.sh (no default features; built with -Zinline-mir=no, so rustc's MIR inliner cannot bypass a stub)

std semantics, with two proof-only selections: A1 align_offset returning usize::MAX (documented as permitted) and G1 Vec::push restricted to its non-growth branch (fails closed; the negative control push_guard_is_in_force must fail on it before the default set runs)
numeric route guard stub in the integer harnesses (fail-closed, checked unreachable for numeric input)
Kani 0.68.0 / CBMC 6.11 and the bundled kissat 4.0.1
real unicode-normalization NFC inside the harnesses that parse strings

claims.claim: TLC checks bounded safety and conditional liveness of GrantLog, a model of the historical single-process, age-based broker_seq recovery design that the current fence protocol superseded (the current protocol is modelled separately in GrantRecovery.tla, which this claim does not cover). The model binds to no current code; its value is the counterexamples it keeps. Recovery needs the stated retry and fairness assumptions.
assumptions: finite configured grant count
strong fairness of operator void
weak fairness of open transaction resolution

claims.claim: TLC checks bounded safety of ConsumeLedger, a model of the superseded pgledger consume and of the tenant migration (AtMostOncePerKey, InFlightRecorded, TenantAtMostOnce, TenantIsolation), with reachability witnesses that the consume path is reachable. The model binds to no current code: the current consume is in server/internal/store/ledger_postgres.go and is not modelled.
assumptions: finite instances, projects and clock
retention at least the capability lifetime in the safe configuration

claims.claim: TLC checks bounded safety and conditional liveness of GrantRecovery, a model of the fence and void recovery of one reservation, with reachability witnesses for both terminal paths. The model binds to no current code, and the deployment barrier against an old writer is an assumption of the safe configuration.
assumptions: one reservation
weak fairness of database resolution and strong fairness of the fence
no permanent database failure

claims.claim: run-tlc.sh pins the SPECIFICATION and the INVARIANT and PROPERTY names of every TLA+ configuration, and requires a reachability witness (a W_ invariant that must be violated) for every passing configuration. This guards against a passing result that checks less than it appears to; it does not show that a witness is the interesting state or that a model matches the code.
assumptions: TLC reports a violated invariant by name
the pin table is reviewed when a configuration changes

claims.claim: The three named API tests exercise void ordering and recovery against real Postgres 16; skips must fail the CI gate.
assumptions: private test schema

database is reachable

claims.claim: With a shared Postgres project Store, an acknowledged revoke is committed before a later use checks revocation on any replica; restart does not restore an older admission view. This is tested behavior. The TLA+ configuration ProjectTx_operational_safe models a guarded use over a finite design model and is not evidence for this tested behavior (no Postgres commit ordering is modelled).
assumptions: revocation enabled
shared Postgres project Store
all use and revoke paths obey WithProjectWrite

claims.claim: With a shared Postgres project Store, a committed prepare is visible to finalize on another replica and after issuer restart; retries read the durable pending row. This is tested behavior. The TLA+ configuration ProjectTx_operational_safe is not evidence for it: the model has no guard-taking finalize, and NoGhostFinalize holds there by definition, so it is not checked in any passing configuration.
assumptions: shared Postgres project Store
prepare and finalize use WithProjectWrite
pending expiry is checked from the authoritative row

claims.claim: Under the caller-selected db_serialized_v1 policy, historical_authorized_as_of_snapshot is satisfied only when every validated receipt carries a body-bound resource-signed authorization ordinal below its grant's authenticated prospective cutoff and at or below the watermark of an authenticated, fresh v2 revocation snapshot for the project. Current revocation still blocks ok, revoked_uses_blocked, authorized and the capstone under every policy; strict, total, legacy v1, stripped, stale or malformed evidence never yields a historical positive. The model theorem covers the claim kernel and support erasure, not the verifier's extraction passes; the order is Averin's database order, not physical action time.
assumptions: honest resource signer signs one ordinal per receipt in its committing transaction
honest revocation signer signs the boundary time and watermark it read
PostgreSQL serializes the project guard row
caller supplies a trustworthy evaluation time and freshness bound

claims.claim: record::seal returns Ok only for a body whose sealed form passes verify_sealed's top-level shape check, domain pin and canon_version pin (SB-29), and checkpoint::seal_checkpoint returns Ok only for a body whose sealed form passes verify_checkpoint_sealed's domain pin and canon_version pin, checked by deterministic property tests and, for the Go server producers that the server test suite reaches (records and checkpoints), by running the real cgo seal in enforce mode across that suite. Not a proof; does not cover nested object shape, unknown checkpoint keys, the checkpoint chain checks of validate_chain, hash or signature validity, or AVERIN_SEAL_SHAPE=shadow, which seals unverifiable records and checkpoints on purpose as a rollback switch.
assumptions: the finite deterministic generator builds the defect classes that matter
the Go suite reaches every producer kind it lists

claims.claim: The averin-verify bundle headline word and exit code equal the report's claim verdict (PASS needs a satisfied requested claim and externally pinned keys; CONSISTENT is the same claim under the bundle's own keys; INSUFFICIENT and FAIL otherwise), the same rule as verifier/claim-verdict.js. A finite differential over the verdict oracle corpus plus an end-to-end test of the binary; not a proof, and it says nothing about whether the claims themselves are right.
targets: JS verifier (same rule, run with node)
assumptions: the report's claims are produced by the claim kernel
the report's ok and keys_externally_pinned are booleans, as every shipped producer emits; on any other value both rules count only the boolean true (differential-tested on one corpus row)
node is on PATH where the differential runs

claims.claim: The Level-3 action_completeness label is never stronger than the claim kernel: a capstone label also requires the kernel's matching complete claim to be satisfied, else it reads claimed_over_manifest. Checked over every case of the verdict oracle corpus (reports built from the checked facts) and by a downgrade unit test; not a proof, and the label still never says more than resource_trust:assumed_truthful allows.
assumptions: the corpus projection from checked facts to report fields matches verify.rs
